body:
Sports day almost did not happen. The field had flooded on Thursday, ___(1)___ the caretaker spent Friday morning sweeping water off the running track.

Ade was the ___(2)___ runner in Year 5, and everybody knew it. What nobody knew was that he had been dreading the relay all week.

“You are on the last leg, ___(3)___?” said Priya, tying her laces.

“Someone has to be,” Ade said.

Priya was the girl ___(4)___ never worried about anything. She had already won the long jump, even though she had landed badly and grazed her knee.

The ___(5)___ crowd made it hard to hear the whistle. Ade took the baton, felt it slip, caught it again and ran. By the final bend he ___(6)___ the boy in the yellow bib.

“___(7)___ going to do it!” shouted Priya.

He did not do it. He came second by half a step, and Mrs Lawson wrote his time on a board beside the finish line. Ade looked at ___(8)___ board for a long time. It was not the win he had wanted, but it was still the best race he had ever run.
